parts.visual:
Phase 1: You are pushing a massive boulder up a steep hill. You have to beg users to try your app. It is exhausting. 
Phase 2: Suddenly, you reach the top of the hill. The boulder starts rolling down the other side so fast it threatens to crush you. Your servers crash because too many people are trying to buy the product. 
The difference between Phase 1 and Phase 2 is Product-Market Fit (PMF).

The Holy Grail:
1. The Definition: Being in a good market with a product that can actually satisfy that market. 
2. The Priority: Before PMF, the only job of the entire company is to find PMF. You do not hire salespeople. You do not optimize the logo. You write code and talk to users until you feel the market physically pulling the product out of your hands.
parts.audio: You can always feel when PMF happens. Before it, you are pushing the product onto the market. After it, the market is pulling the product out of your hands faster than you can build it. It feels like magic.

questions.question: What is the classic 'Sean Ellis Test' for Product-Market Fit?
options: Asking users if they like the logo.

You ask your users: 'How would you feel if you could no longer use this product?' If more than 40% answer 'Very Disappointed', you have PMF. If the answer is 'Somewhat disappointed' or 'I don't care', you do not have PMF.
Testing if the app loads in 2 seconds.
questions.correct_answer: You ask your users: 'How would you feel if you could no longer use this product?' If more than 40% answer 'Very Disappointed', you have PMF. If the answer is 'Somewhat disappointed' or 'I don't care', you do not have PMF.
questions.explanation: If your product disappears and nobody cries, you have failed.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO explaining a mistake. Why did hiring 10 salespeople destroy the company?
questions.tts_text: We had a beautiful product, but nobody was buying it organically. I thought we just had a sales problem. I hired 10 expensive salespeople to push the product. We burned all our cash in 6 months. The problem wasn't sales; we just didn't have PMF.
options: Premature Scaling. Hiring a sales team or spending millions on ads before you have PMF is the #1 cause of startup death. You are pouring gasoline on a fire that hasn't started yet. You cannot out-sell a product nobody wants.
Because the product was too cheap.
questions.correct_answer: Premature Scaling. Hiring a sales team or spending millions on ads before you have PMF is the #1 cause of startup death. You are pouring gasoline on a fire that hasn't started yet. You cannot out-sell a product nobody wants.
questions.explanation: Marketing is an amplifier. If you amplify zero, you get zero.

questions.question: Why do VCs care more about the 'Market' than the 'Product'?
options: A great market will pull the product out of a mediocre team. A terrible market will bankrupt a team of geniuses. If people are literally dying of thirst (great market), they will pay $100 for muddy water in a broken cup (bad product).
questions.correct_answer: A great market will pull the product out of a mediocre team. A terrible market will bankrupt a team of geniuses. If people are literally dying of thirst (great market), they will pay $100 for muddy water in a broken cup (bad product).
questions.explanation: You cannot swim against the current of a bad market.

questions.question: How do you know you definitely do NOT have Product-Market Fit?
options: Word of Mouth is zero. If your users are not actively telling their friends and coworkers to use your product for free, you do not have PMF. True PMF always generates organic, viral growth because the solution is so painful to live without.
questions.correct_answer: Word of Mouth is zero. If your users are not actively telling their friends and coworkers to use your product for free, you do not have PMF. True PMF always generates organic, viral growth because the solution is so painful to live without.
questions.explanation: If they don't love it, they won't share it.
